name: Chronic Exertional Compartment Syndrome
definition: Exercise-induced increase in compartment pressure producing predictable pain, tightness and sometimes neurologic symptoms that resolve with rest.

typical: Reproducible pain/tightness after a specific exercise duration
Possible numbness or weakness during exertion

redFlags.item: Acute severe pain suggesting acute compartment syndrome

investigations.principle: Diagnosis is clinical and may use dynamic compartment pressure testing in specialist practice.
investigations.MRI: MRI can exclude stress injury and alternative pathology.

amber: Persistent confirmed CECS may require fasciotomy after specialist evaluation.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Jangha/Vyayama-related pain phenotype may be documented.

patientEducation.summary: Exercise-induced increase in compartment pressure producing predictable pain, tightness and sometimes neurologic symptoms that resolve with rest.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, severe infection/systemic illness, major trauma, vascular compromise, rapidly escalating pain or other listed red flags.
